## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vipattivāra* (Pvr 2.3) is an analytical section within the *Parivāra*, the concluding book of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The text systematically categorises and correlates the Vinaya disciplinary rules with the categories of "falling away" or failure (*vipatti*) in monastic conduct. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Machine analysis by DharmaNexus registers 105 instances of Pali-internal text reuse across 15 texts, consisting entirely of structural formulas and shared segments recurring within the *Parivāra* itself and related Vinaya catechisms [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial sharing occurs with the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4, 30 matches), followed by the *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 2.8), other sections titled *Vipattivāra* (Pvr 1.11, Pvr 1.3, and Pvr 2.11), the *Adhikaraṇavāra* (Pvr 2.6), *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11), and various other sub-chapters of Parivāra 2 (Pvr 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, 2.5, 2.7, 2.16) and the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā Vinayapiṭaka* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches meet the threshold in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
